headline: The FISHES Act sets deadlines for NOAA to review spending plans from groups seeking federal aid after fishery disasters.
what_it_does: When a state, tribe, or other group asks NOAA for fishery disaster aid, it must submit a plan for how it will spend the money. NOAA now has 10 days to decide if that plan is complete, and must explain in detail what is missing if it is not. NOAA must also tell the requester when the plan is complete. The White House budget office (OMB) may review the plan at the same time, but cannot hold up the existing 90-day deadline for sending the money.

who_it_affects.group: States, tribes, and other groups that apply for fishery disaster aid
who_it_affects.how: They get a quick answer on whether their spending plan is complete and clear details on what to fix if it is not.

who_it_affects.group: Commercial and recreational fishing communities hit by fishery disasters
who_it_affects.how: Aid sent through grantees may reach them with fewer review delays.

who_it_affects.group: NOAA and the Office of Management and Budget
who_it_affects.how: NOAA must meet a 10-day review deadline, and OMB's review cannot delay the 90-day payment timeline.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 4, 2025; the summary does not give a separate start date.
